In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Cox-2 is a bona fide oncogene that plays a role in the development of a wide spectrum of tumors in different species, and that a subset of prosta-noid receptors are oncogenes that promote the development of different tumors in a cell type-specific manner.

Cox-2 and prostanoids have dual functions, both promoting and inhibiting cancer development, depending on the cell type, the type of tumor, and the stage of the disease (for a review, see Subbaramaiah and Dannenberg 2003).
Cox-2 is a bona fide oncogene, and that the expression and/or function of Cox-2, PGE, and EP2/EP4 is a critical determinant for the malignant phenotype of cancer cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Cox-2 and its prostanoid products regulate, and are themselves regulated by, pathways that play critical roles in oncogenesis, and that these pathways can be targeted for the development of new cancer therapeutics.
the Cox-2 and prostanoid pathways are involved in oncogenesis and that this involvement may be mediated by their interaction with other pathways.

prostanoid signaling is an essential part of the crosstalk between oncogenic signaling pathways.
